description: Shared scrub-audit agreement fixture (ticket 51). One contract for the two implementations of the privacy audit: the Rust byte scanner in src-tauri/src/core/scrub.rs (the authority, it redacts) and the TypeScript match scanner in src/core/scrub.ts (the user-facing warning before a report is copied). Both tests assert the same violation count for every input. Inputs are restricted to cases with unambiguous, disjoint hazards: where two hazards share one enclosing region (a field name twice in one tag, a hazard-shaped value inside a field-name tag, two field names in tag-less text) the Rust scanner merges them into one span while the TypeScript scanner reports every regex match - a deliberate, documented divergence that never changes whether text is judged hazardous. A bounded twelve-hex run is flagged by BOTH implementations (twelve-digit-run): over-detection is the safe bias for a privacy audit, and is not a divergence.
